summary: Joseph Toussaint Reinaud worked in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology, having studied under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. He held posts at INALCO from 1838, the Société Asiatique from 1852, and the Bibliothèque nationale de France from 1854.
Joseph Walser is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He pursued his education under the instruction of Isshi Yamada, Adolf von Wuertenburg, and David S. Pacini.
Josho Nozawa (1907–1993) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Susumu Yamaguchi and held a professorship at Koyasan University, attested in 1950.

Joshua T. Katz is a linguist who studied at the Dalton School, Yale University (~1987–1991), the University of Oxford (~1991–1993), and Harvard University (~1993–1998). He served as a faculty member at Princeton University from 1998 to 2022.
Joshua W. C. Cutler specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under the traditional teacher Geshe Wangyal and held a post at the Tibetan Buddhist Learning Center, attested in 2004.

Josiah Royce (1855–1916) was a philosopher who studied at UC Berkeley (~1871–1875) and Johns Hopkins University (~1876–1878). He held academic posts at UC Berkeley (~1878–1882) and Harvard University (~1882–1916).

José Ignacio Cabezón works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, having earned degrees from Caltech and the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa. He held posts at Iliff School of Theology, the University of Denver, and UC Santa Barbara.
Jotika Khur-Yearn is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He earned his PhD at SOAS University of London, studying under doctoral supervisor Kate Crosby (attested 2012).

Jowita Kramer is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who studied at the University of Hamburg and LMU Munich. She held positions at Oxford, LMU Munich, Heidelberg, UC Berkeley, Göttingen, and EPHE.

Joy Brennan specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Chicago, where she studied under Paul Mendes-Flohr, Richard Rosengarten, and Constance Furey, and studied with traditional teacher Diane Martin.
Juan Wu is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed her PhD at Cardiff University under the doctoral supervision of Max Deeg, attested in 2012.

Judit Törzsök is an Indologist who studied at Eötvös Loránd University and the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. She held posts at the University of Lille (~2001–2017) and became professor at the École Pratique des Hautes Études in 2018.

Judith Simmer-Brown is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Western Washington University and under Chögyam Trungpa. In 1977, she became chair of the Religious Studies Department at Naropa University.

Juhn Y. Ahn is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He earned his PhD from the University of California, Berkeley in 2007 and was attested in 2019 as an Associate Professor at the University of Michigan.
Juhyung Rhi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and art history who completed his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley. In 1992, he became Professor of Art History at Seoul National University.

Juichiro Tanabe works in religious studies. He studied at the University of Bradford from 2000 to 2001 and as a PhD candidate attested in 2010, and also studied under traditional teacher Richard Hunn.

Jules Barthélemy-Saint-Hilaire (1805–1895) was a scholar in philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Bourbon College and Lycée Louis-le-Grand. He held posts at the Collège de France (1838–1852) and the Académie des Sciences Morales et Politiques (~1839–1895).

Jules Bloch (1880–1953) was an Indologist and linguist educated at EPHE, ENLOV, and the University of Paris. He held positions at EPHE, ENLOV, the University of Lyon, and served as Chair of Sanskrit at the Collège de France (1936–1951).

Jules Brooks Levinson works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, earning his PhD from the University of Virginia in 1994 under Jeffrey Hopkins. He founded the Light of Berotsana Translation Group (1999) and taught at Hamline University (attested 1996).

Jules Michelet (1798–1874) was a historian who studied at Lycée Charlemagne (1812–1816). He held posts at Collège-lycée Jacques-Decour (1822), École Normale Supérieure (1827), Archives nationales (1830–1852), and the Collège de France (1838–1852).
